name: AIS-catcher
description: Turns an RTL-SDR or similar dongle and a small computer into an AIS receiver with a web map, and feeds AISHub or the commercial networks. Range is line of sight, a few tens of nautical miles.
section: Raw feeds and your own receiver

name: AISHub
description: A pooled raw AIS feed and API that you get access to by contributing a live feed from your own receiver. Live data only.
section: Raw feeds and your own receiver

name: aisstream.io
description: A live global WebSocket feed of AIS messages, filtered by bounding box or MMSI, with GitHub sign-in. No history, three connections per account, and connections must come from a server rather than a browser.
section: Raw feeds and your own receiver

name: AMSA vessel traffic data
description: Monthly AIS shapefiles for the Australian search-and-rescue region, at roughly hourly positions. Good free history for the Indo-Pacific approaches.

name: BarentsWatch AIS API
description: Developer API over the Norwegian AIS feed with about two weeks of history. Norway only.

name: Danish AIS data
description: Daily files of AIS for Danish waters, the approach to the Baltic. The shore network moved to the Danish Emergency Management Agency; historical files are supplied on application.

name: Digitraffic Marine
description: Live AIS over REST and MQTT plus Portnet port-call schedules, with commercial use allowed. Finland and the northern Baltic only; requests need a `Digitraffic-User` header.

name: Global Fishing Watch APIs
description: Vessel search, events, presence grids from 2012 to about four days ago, and radar detections through a documented API with a Python client. No commercial licence is offered.

name: Global Fishing Watch map
description: Tracks from 2012, port visits, encounters, loitering, AIS gaps and radar detections for the whole world. Built around fishing and carrier vessels, and about three days behind live.
section: Live maps with a free tier

name: Kystverket AIS
description: A live API for the Norwegian economic zone with no registration, plus historical files back to 2005 that include Norway's own satellite AIS. Small fishing and leisure craft are excluded, and full history needs an application.

name: MarineCadastre vessel traffic
description: Bulk US-waters AIS from 2009 to the previous year, filtered to one position a minute, with GeoParquet files from 2024 onward. The deepest free raw AIS archive anywhere, but US waters only.

name: MarineRadar
description: Live terrestrial and satellite AIS for more than 100,000 vessels with route playback, on the web and in mobile apps. Subscription prices are not published.
section: Live maps with a free tier

name: MarineTraffic
description: The largest crowd-sourced AIS map, with vessel pages, port calls and photos. Free accounts see about a day of track and no port calls or ownership; Kpler has owned it since March 2023 and the free tier has narrowed since.
section: Live maps with a free tier

name: MyShipTracking
description: Terrestrial AIS map with a credit-based API and a free trial key. Coverage is near-shore only.
section: Live maps with a free tier

name: OpenCPN
description: A chart plotter that shows AIS from your receiver over real charts and keeps a local log. Useful for offline analysis of your own feed.
section: Raw feeds and your own receiver

name: ShipAtlas
description: Satellite AIS positions, recent port calls and a sea-route calculator. The free tier is capped at ten satellite position views.
section: Live maps with a free tier

name: Shipinfo.net
description: AIS map with waterway and port-congestion analytics and Northern Sea Route ice layers. Operated from Russia, so think about what you query from a case machine.
section: Live maps with a free tier

name: ShipXplorer
description: AIS map fed by hobbyist receivers, from the company behind ShipSpotting. Hosting a receiver earns a premium account.
section: Live maps with a free tier

name: Tradlinx vessel tracking
description: Latest position, destination and identifiers for a ship by name, MMSI, IMO or call sign, with no account. Near-shore receivers only; satellite coverage is in the paid Ocean Visibility product.
section: Live maps with a free tier

name: VesselFinder
description: Live map and vessel particulars with the cheapest paid route to longer tracks (3, 7 or 90 days by tier). Its terms forbid scraping and building datasets.
section: Live maps with a free tier

name: ABS Record
description: Class records for ABS-classed ships.

name: Black Sea MoU
description: Inspection records for the Black Sea states. The public database is developed and hosted by the Russian Federation, and may not load from every network.

name: ClassNK Register of Ships
description: Class records for the Japanese society's large fleet.

name: DNV Vessel Register
description: Class status, surveys and certificates for ships classed by DNV.

name: Equasis
owner: EMSA and a consortium of maritime administrations
description: Particulars, registered owner and managers, class, P&I cover and port state inspections for most merchant ships, and from 2026 a record of ship-to-ship transfers. The first stop for any vessel.

name: IMO GISIS
description: The IMO's own ship and company records: name and flag history, IMO company numbers and registered addresses. The public modules need a free IMO web account.

name: Indian Ocean MoU
description: Inspection and detention data for the Indian Ocean region.

name: ITU MARS ship station search
description: Looks up a ship by MMSI, call sign, name or distress-beacon identity and returns the administration that registered it. The quickest check that an MMSI matches a flag.

name: Liberian Registry
description: Public vessel and certificate lookups for the Liberian flag.

name: Marshall Islands Registry
description: Public information and lookups for the Marshall Islands flag.

name: Panama Maritime Authority
description: The world's largest flag registry; its public pages hold registry notices and verification services.

name: Ships IO
description: Crowd-sourced database of about 160,000 large ships with technical and commercial details, linked companies, yards and parts. Cheap enough for individuals, but check its claims against Equasis.

name: ShipSpotting
description: Dated, crowd-sourced ship photos, useful for confirming a hull, a livery or a name change. Browsing is free; uploading needs an account.

name: Superyachts.com Top 100
description: Rankings and owner searches for the largest yachts, useful in sanctions and asset-tracing work.

name: THETIS (Paris MoU)
description: Inspection and detention records for ships calling in Europe, Canada and Russia's European ports.

name: Tokyo MoU APCIS
description: Asia-Pacific inspection records in near real time. The database is hosted in Vladivostok.

name: USCG PSIX
description: Weekly snapshot of Coast Guard records: particulars, inspections, deficiencies and detentions for ships in US waters.

name: ArcNautical
description: Screens one IMO number against the OFAC, EU, UK and UN lists without an account, states which lists it could reach, and offers a keyless JSON endpoint. Launched in 2026; cross-check its result against OpenSanctions and the official lists.

name: Combined IUU Vessel List
description: Every regional fisheries organisation's list of vessels caught fishing illegally, merged with Interpol notices, with name and flag history, alerts and a spreadsheet download.

name: EU Sanctions Map
description: Every EU sanctions regime with the legal acts and the listed persons, entities and vessels.

name: FAO Global Record
description: The Global Record of Fishing Vessels, with a unique vessel identifier and quick search by IMO, MMSI or call sign.

name: GLEIF LEI search
description: Legal entity identifiers with registered addresses and parent relationships for companies that have one. Good for banks, traders and larger shipowners.

name: ICCAT Record of Vessels
owner: International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas
description: Authorised vessels and the Atlantic IUU list.

name: ICIJ Offshore Leaks Database
description: Companies, officers and addresses from the Panama Papers, Paradise Papers, Pandora Papers and related leaks. The usual way into offshore shipowning structures.

name: IOTC vessel records
description: Authorised and IUU vessel lists for the Indian Ocean.

name: KSE Institute Shadow Fleet Tracker
description: Monthly reports on Russian seaborne oil exports and the tankers carrying them. Reports and data downloads rather than a vessel search.

name: OCCRP Aleph
owner: Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project
description: Searchable archive of company registries, leaks and documents. Some collections are open only to journalists.

name: OFAC Sanctions List Search
description: The official search of US designations, including vessels by IMO number.

name: OpenCorporates
description: The largest open database of companies and officers, with searches free on the web and the API and bulk data paid. Free API access is available to public-benefit projects on application.

name: OpenSanctions
description: Consolidated sanctions and politically exposed person data from more than a hundred sources, with vessels as entities matched to IMO numbers, flag histories and shadow-fleet tags. Commercial use needs a licence.

name: Rendezvous
access_note: early access; terms not yet published, 2026-10
description: An open platform on the Baltic shadow fleet whose tracker scores vessels with a calibrated machine-learning model over AIS silences, encounters, flag history and port calls, alongside commodity-flow data and maps of sensitive infrastructure. Early-stage, with deployments around the Gulf of Finland and the Kerch Strait; the technology page explains the method.

name: UANI tanker tracker
description: A running list of several hundred tankers linked to Iranian oil. UANI is an advocacy group, so confirm against the official lists before you rely on an entry.

name: UK Sanctions List
owner: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
description: The UK's consolidated designations, including ships specified under the Russia regime.

name: UN Security Council Consolidated List
description: All individuals, entities and vessels listed by the Council's sanctions committees.

name: WCPFC Record of Fishing Vessels
owner: Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission
description: Public search and CSV download of vessels authorised to fish in the western and central Pacific, with photos and the option to include deleted records.

name: Bellingcat Ship Detection Tool
description: Counts and plots ships in Sentinel-1 radar imagery for any area and date range, including ships with AIS off. Runs in Google Earth Engine; Bellingcat's 2023 guide explains the method.

name: Capella Open Data
description: Sample high-resolution radar scenes on AWS. Capella has been owned by IonQ since July 2025.

name: Copernicus Browser
owner: European Space Agency for the European Commission
description: Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery with search, time-lapse and download. Sentinel-1 is back to a six-day revisit since the 1C and 1D satellites came into service in 2025 and 2026.

name: Copernicus Data Space
description: The APIs behind the browser (STAC, OData and processing) for pulling Sentinel data into your own tools.

name: EOS LandViewer
description: Browser for Sentinel, Landsat and some commercial imagery with analysis tools; the free tier allows a small number of scenes a month.

name: Global Fishing Watch data portal
description: Downloads of radar vessel detections matched to AIS (from 2017), fishing effort and other derived datasets. The radar layer is the simplest global view of unmatched, likely dark, vessels.

name: NASA FIRMS
description: Active fire and thermal anomaly detections, including flaring at offshore platforms and fires at sea.

name: NASA Worldview
description: Same-day, low-resolution global imagery from MODIS and VIIRS, enough to see weather, smoke, ice and large slicks.

name: OpenAerialMap
description: Openly licensed aerial and drone imagery uploaded by mappers and responders, much of it very high resolution and much of it after disasters. Patchy, but where it exists it beats satellite imagery.

name: SkyFi
description: Marketplace for buying archive imagery or new tasking from several satellite operators by the scene, for people who need one picture rather than a contract.

name: Skylight
description: Maritime monitoring platform that fuses AIS, radar and optical detections into alerts, free to governments, regional bodies and NGOs working on illegal fishing and maritime security.

name: SkyTruth Cerulean
description: Oil slicks detected in Sentinel-1 radar, with the likely source vessel or platform suggested from AIS, through a map and an API. Vessel attribution runs a few days behind.

name: Umbra Open Data
description: Very high-resolution radar imagery of about twenty fixed sites, some of them ports, with no sign-up. A good way to learn what commercial SAR can show.

name: Vantor Discover
description: Browse previews of the commercial high-resolution archive for free; buying a scene is quote-based. The portal kept its Maxar address after the 2025 rename.

name: Vantor Open Data Program
description: High-resolution before-and-after imagery released for major disasters as a catalogue on AWS. Event-driven rather than on demand, and non-commercial use only.

name: VIIRS Boat Detection
owner: Earth Observation Group, Colorado School of Mines
description: Nightly detections of lit fishing boats from the VIIRS day-night band, useful for squid and other light-attracting fleets.

name: Container Port Performance Index
owner: World Bank and S&P Global Market Intelligence
description: Annual ranking of about 400 container ports by time in port, built from AIS, with the report and the data file for download.

name: Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker
description: LNG terminals and gas pipelines worldwide, with ownership and status, downloadable after a short form.

name: IMF PortWatch
owner: International Monetary Fund with the University of Oxford
description: Daily port calls and trade volume estimates for about 1,800 ports and transit counts for the main chokepoints, updated weekly, with an ArcGIS API. The figures are modelled from AIS and get revised.

name: Marine Regions
description: Exclusive economic zones, territorial seas and other maritime boundaries as downloadable geodata. The reference layer for "whose waters is this ship in".

name: NGA World Port Index
description: Publication 150: location, depths, facilities and services for several thousand ports, as a spreadsheet or GIS layer.

name: OpenInfraMap
description: Power lines, telecoms, oil and gas infrastructure drawn from OpenStreetMap, including offshore platforms and pipelines.

name: Port Optimizer
owner: Port of Los Angeles with Wabtec
description: Volumes, forecasts and container tracking for the port of Los Angeles. One of the few ports that publishes forward-looking data.

name: SubTel Forum Cable Map
description: A second cable map that also shows the cable-ship fleet and planned systems.

name: TeleGeography Submarine Cable Map
description: The standard interactive map of submarine cables and landing stations, covering 694 systems in its 2026 edition.

name: UNCTAD Liner Shipping Connectivity Index
description: Quarterly index of how well each country and port is connected to container shipping networks, inside the UNCTADstat data centre.

name: BIC container owner codes
description: The register behind the first three letters of every container number: who owns or operates the box.

name: Drewry World Container Index
description: Weekly spot container rates on the main east-west routes. The headline figures are free; the detail is a subscription.

name: Eurostat Comext
description: EU trade in goods at eight-digit product detail by partner country and month.

name: Freightos Baltic Index
description: Daily container spot index by lane; headline rates are free and the full series is paid.

name: ImportYeti
description: US import bills of lading searchable by company, supplier and product, free with limits on how much detail you see. The free way into the data Panjiva and ImportGenius sell.

name: ITC Trade Map
description: Trade flows, tariffs and market indicators by product and country, with company directories for some markets.

name: OEC
description: Visual explorer of trade flows by country and product, built on Comtrade and national data. Good for a first picture; check the numbers at source.

name: Open Supply Hub
description: An open database of production facilities with names, addresses and the brands that list them. Search and downloads are free; the API is paid.

name: Resource Trade Earth
description: Trade in natural resources (fuels, metals, agricultural goods) by country pair, with maps and downloads.

name: SeaRates container tracking
description: Tracks by container, bill of lading or booking number across most carriers and shows the carrying vessel's position. Free lookups are limited without an account.

name: ShipsGo
description: Multi-carrier container tracking with a few free lookups, then per-shipment credits and an API.

name: Track-Trace
description: Sends a container number to the right page of about 170 carriers. Nothing stored, nothing to sign up for.

name: UN Comtrade
description: Bilateral trade by product code for almost every country, with a free API key subject to daily limits.

name: USA Trade Online
description: US imports and exports at ten-digit detail by country, district and port.

name: WITS
description: Trade and tariff data with bulk download and an API, drawing on Comtrade and tariff databases.

name: ACLED
owner: Armed Conflict Location and Event Data
description: Coded political violence and protest events worldwide, including attacks on ports and shipping, downloadable after registration.

name: Eyes on Russia map
description: Verified, geolocated incidents from the war in Ukraine, including Black Sea and port events, built with C4ADS.

name: GDELT
description: Machine-coded records of news events and mentions worldwide, downloadable in bulk or through BigQuery. Noisy, but a quick way to see what was reported about a port or sea area on a given day.

name: IMB
description: Runs the 24-hour Piracy Reporting Centre that collects attack reports worldwide and publishes quarterly statistics and an incident map.

name: Liveuamap
description: Geolocated news events, including strikes on shipping and ports in the Black Sea and the Red Sea. Ad-supported, with an optional ad-free subscription.

name: MARA
description: Our maritime security intelligence platform: round-the-clock monitoring of security incidents with alerts, intelligence reports, daily hot spots and country and port indices. Feedback and the public roadmap are on GitHub.

name: Maritime Cyber Attack Database
owner: NHL Stenden University of Applied Sciences, Netherlands
description: About 300 cyber incidents against ships, ports and maritime companies since 2001, with a map filterable by victim, attacker, country and year.

name: Maritime Security Centre Indian Ocean
description: Threat assessments, incident updates and voluntary registration for ships transiting the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean. The successor to MSCHOA, the Horn of Africa centre.

name: MICA Center
description: The Brest centre that hosts MDAT-GoG, the French and British reporting and advisory service for the Gulf of Guinea, and publishes annual and weekly maritime security reports.

name: NGA Maritime Safety Information
description: Navigation warnings, broadcast warnings and the Anti-Shipping Activity Messages (ASAM) database, a geocoded record of attacks and suspicious approaches going back to the 1980s.

name: ONI Worldwide Threat to Shipping
description: Weekly summary of threats and incidents by region, compiled from the reporting centres and open sources.

name: Phantom Tide
access_note: Starter tier; higher tiers exist, prices not published, 2026-10
description: Analyst dashboard that ranks hotspots where vessel tracks, aircraft, navigation warnings, weather, satellite detections and GNSS interference overlap, with a notebook and area reports. A hosted app with closed source; the public repository holds the docs and release notes.

name: ReCAAP ISC
description: Incident reports, weekly and annual statistics and a searchable map for piracy and armed robbery in Asia. The dashboard needs a free account.

name: UKMTO
description: Advisories and incident reports for the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Arabian Sea and the Gulf, and the voluntary reporting scheme ships use there.

name: Baidu Maps
description: Coverage and street views of Chinese ports. It uses its own shifted coordinate system, so convert before you compare positions.

name: Bing Maps
description: A second aerial imagery source, often from a different date than Google's, with bird's-eye views of many ports.

name: Copernicus Marine
description: Ocean current, wave, temperature and sea-ice datasets, for drift and feasibility analysis.

name: DualMaps
description: Road map, aerial view and Street View side by side for one point.

name: earth.nullschool
description: Animated global wind, ocean current and wave fields, with a time slider.

name: EMODnet
description: European marine data: bathymetry, human activities (cables, pipelines, wind farms, dredging) and more as map layers and downloads.

name: GEBCO
description: The global bathymetry grid. Can a ship of this draught be where its AIS says it is?

name: GeoNames
description: Gazetteer of place names with coordinates and alternate spellings, for matching ports named in several languages.

name: Google Earth
description: The desktop Pro version has a historical imagery slider, the easiest way to watch a berth, a terminal or a shipyard change over years.

name: KartaView
description: Crowd-sourced street-level photos, useful where Street View has nothing.

name: Navionics ChartViewer
description: Worldwide nautical charts with depths and anchorages in the browser.

name: NOAA ENC Viewer
description: US electronic navigational charts in the browser.

name: OpenSeaMap
description: A nautical overlay on OpenStreetMap: buoys, lights, harbours and anchorages.

name: OpenStreetMap
description: Community-mapped berths, terminals, piers and port infrastructure with tags you can query.

name: PeakFinder
description: Draws the mountain skyline from any viewpoint, which geolocates many coastal photographs.

name: WikiMapia
description: Crowd-labelled places, including industrial sites, terminals and naval facilities that official maps leave blank.

name: Windy
description: Wind, wave, swell and current forecasts and recent history from several models. A quick check on whether a claimed speed or route makes sense.

name: Yandex Maps
description: The best coverage and street panoramas for Russian and Central Asian ports.

name: Zoom Earth
description: Near-real-time weather satellite imagery and storm tracks that affect shipping routes.

name: Altana
description: Supply chain network mapping across shipment and corporate records.

name: Ambrey
description: Maritime security advisories, intelligence and armed guarding.

name: Datalastic
description: A developer-oriented AIS and vessel data API, one of the cheaper paid routes to programmatic positions. The site refuses some automated and overseas requests.

name: Descartes Datamyne
description: Import and export records for the Americas and beyond.

name: Dryad Global
description: Maritime risk intelligence and advisories, with some free weekly commentary.

name: HawkEye 360
description: Radio-frequency geolocation and maritime domain awareness products for governments.

name: ICEYE
description: Tasked high-resolution radar imagery and dark vessel detection products.

name: ImportGenius
description: US and other customs shipment records with published subscription plans.

name: Kharon
description: Research and data on sanctions, export controls and the networks around designated parties.

name: Kpler
description: Commodity flows, cargo tracking and the combined MarineTraffic, FleetMon and Spire AIS feeds, sold as a platform and as data.

name: Linerlytica
description: Container shipping market analysis and port congestion tracking.

name: Lloyd's List Intelligence
description: Seasearcher vessel database, risk and compliance screening, casualty records and the Lloyd's List news service.

name: Panjiva
description: Bills of lading and shipment records for many countries, with company profiles and network views.

name: Planet
description: Daily optical imagery of the whole land surface and coasts, plus the Sentinel Hub APIs under the Planet Insights Platform.

name: Pole Star Global
description: PurpleTRAC sanctions screening and fleet monitoring, widely used by banks and traders.

name: Risk Intelligence
description: The MaRisk system of port and sea-area threat assessments.

name: S&P Global Market Intelligence
description: Sea-web and the Maritime Portal (the ship database descended from Lloyd's Register-Fairplay), satellite AIS from the former ORBCOMM business, and Panjiva trade data.

name: Sayari
description: Corporate ownership graph built from public records in many jurisdictions, with trade and sanctions risk screening.

name: Sea-Intelligence
description: Liner schedule reliability and container market research.

name: Sourcemap
description: Supplier mapping and traceability for regulatory due diligence. The free edition we once listed is gone.

name: Starboard Maritime Intelligence
description: Vessel risk and dark activity analytics aimed at governments and fisheries agencies in the Pacific and beyond.

name: SynMax
description: Theia, a dark vessel detection platform combining radar and optical imagery with AIS.

name: TankerTrackers.com
description: Tanker movements, floating storage and sanctioned oil flows from imagery and AIS. Retail tiers are closed to new subscribers.

name: Unseenlabs
description: Geolocation of ships from their radio-frequency emissions, independent of AIS.

name: Volza
description: Export and import shipment data for a large set of countries, sold by subscription.

name: Vortexa
description: Cargo-level tracking of oil, gas and refined products, with analytics on floating storage and shadow fleet flows.

name: Windward
description: AI risk scores for vessels and companies, dark activity and sanctions compliance workflows.

name: Worldwide AIS Network
description: Live and regional AIS feeds over REST, WebSocket and raw NMEA, with a free data sample for evaluation. A smaller alternative to the Kpler and S&P feeds.

name: bbox finder
description: Draw a box on a map and get its coordinates in the format an API wants, which is the quickest way to set up an aisstream.io or Copernicus filter.

name: Bellingcat auto-archiver
description: Archives web pages, posts and media from a spreadsheet of URLs, with hashes and timestamps, so that a vessel page or a port notice is preserved before it changes.

name: cue-kit
description: Turns a video URL or file into extracted frames and a timestamped transcript that a language model can actually read, with a bundled Claude Code skill for asking questions about footage. Alpha, and useful for port and vessel videos.

name: equasis-cli
description: Looks up vessels, port state inspections, ownership history and company fleets in Equasis from the command line, an interactive shell or Python, handles batches of hundreds of ships, and flags renames, reflagging, detentions and missing P&I cover. Needs your own free Equasis account; install from PyPI or this repository only.

name: gfw-api-python-client
description: Official Python client for the Global Fishing Watch APIs: vessel search, events and presence grids straight into pandas.

name: Hunchly
description: Browser extension that captures and hashes every page you visit during an investigation, which is the evidence trail you want when a vessel page changes after you cite it.

name: Kepler.gl
description: Browser tool that plots millions of points from a CSV or GeoParquet file with a time slider, which is how we first look at a bulk AIS download.

name: pyais
description: Python library that decodes and encodes AIS NMEA sentences, the first thing you need to read a raw feed or a receiver log.

name: QGIS
description: Desktop GIS for laying AIS points, EEZ boundaries, bathymetry and satellite imagery on one map. Plugins pull Copernicus and Vantor open data in directly.

name: Shodan
description: Search engine for internet-exposed devices, including ships' satellite terminals and port systems. Its old AIS ship tracker is gone and AIS data is now sold only as a bulk dataset.

name: SunCalc
description: Sun position and shadow length for any place and time, for dating or placing a photograph of a ship or a port.

name: VESSA dataset
owner: Pablo Rangel and colleagues, Brazilian Navy Research Institute and UFRJ
description: More than 200,000 labelled vessel images in 25 categories for training detectors and classifiers, published on Zenodo in November 2025.

name: AIS datasets on Kaggle
description: Practice datasets of AIS positions uploaded by users, mostly copies of public releases such as MarineCadastre and the Danish files, for learning to clean and plot tracks.

name: Allianz Safety and Shipping Review
description: The annual review of ship losses, casualties and risk trends, the standard open reference on what goes wrong at sea and where.

name: Atlas Bear Academy
description: Our professional development programmes in maritime security and supply chain intelligence.

name: awesome-osint
description: The largest general OSINT list, with about 1,450 entries. Its maritime section is three lines long, which is why this list exists.

name: Bellingcat Online Investigation Toolkit
description: Hundreds of tool pages with cost, requirements, limitations and ethical notes, including a maritime section updated in 2026. Our pointer for general OSINT tools.

name: C4ADS
description: Reports on illicit networks, sanctions evasion and the shadow fleet, with the data-driven method laid out in each one.

name: Deep Dive by Rae Baker
description: Maritime OSINT guides from the author of *Deep Dive*, including a maritime patterning framework, port analysis and a Raspberry Pi AIS receiver build.

name: Free government nautical charts
description: A maintained list of the national hydrographic offices that give their charts away, with links.

name: GIJN: Tracking Ships at Sea
description: A reporter's guide to vessel tracking, ownership and imagery, with case examples.

name: ODIS Catalogue of Sources
description: A searchable catalogue of more than 3,000 ocean data and information sources, for finding the agency that holds the dataset you need.

name: OSINT Framework
description: A categorised tree of general OSINT tools with registration and pricing markers and a weekly link check.

name: Peering Beyond the Clouds
description: The 2023 guide to finding ships in Sentinel-1 radar imagery with the Ship Detection Tool, and the best short introduction to SAR for analysts.

name: Setting up an SDR AIS receiver with AIS-catcher
description: A step-by-step guide to building your own AIS receiver from a software-defined radio dongle, written by a commercial feed provider.

name: Shipmap.org
owner: Kiln and the UCL Energy Institute
description: An animated map of the world's merchant shipping over one year, built from 2012 AIS data. Old, but the best single picture of how trade moves for a classroom.

name: Summer School on Illicit Trade
description: The annual summer school where this list gets used and tested each year, with sessions on maritime and supply-chain OSINT.

name: The Organized Crime Index
owner: Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime
description: Country scores for criminal markets and actors, from arms and drugs to human trafficking, with the methodology published. Useful context for any illicit trade case.

name: UN AIS Handbook
owner: UN Committee of Experts on Big Data, AIS Task Team
description: The method handbook for cleaning and analysing AIS data for statistics, with worked examples. Most pages date from 2020 to 2023, but the fundamentals have not moved.

name: World Factbook Archive
owner: MilkMp, a community project not affiliated with the CIA
description: Every edition of the CIA World Factbook from 1990 to 2025 as a searchable site, a database and a free offline app, after the CIA discontinued the Factbook on 4 February 2026. Its Intelligence Atlas layers submarine cables, shipping routes, chokepoints and EEZ boundaries over the country data.
